title: Blessed Virgin Mary of the Rosary
short_summary: The Blessed Virgin Mary of the Rosary is kept in the Dominican calendar as a feast that turns Marian devotion toward contemplation of Christ and the mysteries of salvation.
key_facts: The Dominican Calendarium keeps the Blessed Virgin Mary of the Rosary as a feast on October 7.
The Order of Preachers connects this feast with the Church's celebration of the wonders of salvation.
Saint John Paul II described the Rosary as a simple and profound prayer within the Christian life.
The Rosary is Marian, but its meditation is centered on Christ.
This Dominican profile is local or proper in the app; the general U.S. calendar remains primary.

sections.heading: A Dominican Marian feast
sections.body: The Rosary has a deep place in Dominican devotion. In this feast, the Order honors Mary while directing prayer toward the saving mysteries of her Son.

sections.heading: Meditating on Christ
sections.body: The Rosary is not a substitute for the Gospel. It is a way of lingering with the mysteries of Christ's life, death, and Resurrection in the company of Mary.

sections.heading: Prayer that forms attention
sections.body: The repeated prayers of the Rosary are meant to steady the heart for contemplation. They train attention toward the Lord rather than toward spiritual distraction.

sections.heading: A proper Dominican feast
sections.body: The app presents the Dominican feast as a proper calendar observance for Dominican users. It does not make the observance the primary general U.S. calendar day.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Marian devotion ordered to Jesus
catholic_connection_sections.body: Catholic devotion to Mary is faithful when it leads more deeply into the mystery of Christ and the Gospel.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Prayer with the Church
catholic_connection_sections.body: The Rosary belongs to the Church's living devotional tradition and invites the faithful to receive the mysteries of salvation with Mary's faith.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Contemplation and mission
catholic_connection_sections.body: For Dominicans, contemplation is never closed in on itself. Prayer prepares the heart to speak and live the truth of Christ with charity.
